title: DNS Helps Agents Find Services While Applications Enforce Authority

cover.subtitle: Discovery finds services. Authorization controls actions.
cover.visual: Two separate tiny panels: discovery compass and policy gate. No arrows suggesting DNS automatically grants permission.

sections.name: 01-discovery-locates-an-endpoint-without-granting-an-action
sections.heading: Discovery locates an endpoint without granting an action
sections.scene: A domain resolves to an agent endpoint and public card. A separate locked action endpoint requires authorization. Discovery arrow stops before the permission gate.
sections.alt: Discovery locates an endpoint without granting an action.

sections.name: 02-domain-control-supports-a-claim-with-a-defined-scope
sections.heading: Domain control supports a claim with a defined scope
sections.scene: An administrator publishes a service-specific TXT challenge. A verifier links only the named domain and service account, with no blanket authority badge.
sections.alt: Domain control supports a claim with a defined scope.

sections.name: 03-authorization-checks-bind-identity-to-a-permitted-operation
sections.heading: Authorization checks bind identity to a permitted operation
sections.scene: An authenticated request carries a resource-specific token through a server permission check. Read operation passes, transfer operation stops at a separate approval gate.
sections.alt: Authorization checks bind identity to a permitted operation.

sections.name: 04-rotation-and-revocation-must-reach-the-enforcement-system
sections.heading: Rotation and revocation must reach the enforcement system
sections.scene: A discovery record retires in one lane while credential revocation occurs at a resource server in another lane. A denied request verifies the revoked permission.
sections.alt: Rotation and revocation must reach the enforcement system.

purpose: Initial illustration plan. The final image review manifest records actual asset hashes and visual revisions.
